implementation_state: The upstream contracts this node was blocked on are now closed: ACCOUNT, NEWAPI, I2, I3 and I4 all pass their gates, so the blocked_by set is emptied and the node is no longer waiting on upstream. One of its three own gates has moved. Backend lifecycle ownership is no longer wholly unmet: the account reconciler now has a real production caller in AppState::reconcile_accounts, which is the first of the four engines to leave the fixture world. The other three engines — MigrationExecutor, TakeoverStore, and the rollback path — still have no caller, and none of them has a desktop command or GUI control that triggers it. The account caller is itself not yet triggered by anything a user can press, so nothing here is a product surface yet. Real account/NewAPI/migration/takeover surfaces and the product confirmation and rollback UI remain unmet. The core has the pieces a surface would need — durable ownership with compare-and-swap, conflict resolution applied on release, accurate rollback reporting, and an account reconciler that publishes outcomes rather than only successes — and a product surface may be built on those once the confirmation semantics are agreed.
unblock_condition: Close the Account, NewAPI, I2, I3, and I4 lifecycle contracts before adding user-facing controls.
notes: No placeholder control is treated as a product lifecycle.

No longer blocked on upstream: ACCOUNT, NEWAPI, I2, I3, and I4 all pass their gates and their blocked_by sets are empty. The status is PARTIAL because its own three gates are unmet, not because it is waiting on another node.
